_comment: The English UI strings: the reference every site/i18n/<locale>/strings.json translates. Partials use them as {{t:key}} (HTML) or {{tj:key}} (JavaScript); scripts/build_site.py uses the rest. {name} is filled in by the generator and must stay in every translation. The site.json nav is translated gettext style in each locale's "nav" object, keyed by the English text. See scripts/site_i18n.py.

ui.catches.legend.text: The scores are our judgement, 1 to 5, drawn from published studies of agent-written code and from our own agent runs. Nobody has measured these rates directly. The list is sorted by likelihood times severity.
ui.catches.measured: Every TypeScript example on the list passes tsc --strict with no errors. Each one is also checked against a fully configured project: every compiler flag stricter than --strict, plus typescript-eslint strictTypeChecked. For {none} of the {count} cases, nothing in that setup catches it. A compiler flag that is off by default catches {flag}, and a lint rule catches {lint}. A project has to turn each of those on, and an agent can turn it off again. In Glyph none of them is a setting.
ui.catches.breakdown: There are {total} checked cases: {count} TypeScript cases, {trap_count} JavaScript traps that do not exist in Glyph, and {gap_cases} holes Glyph does not close yet. Glyph refuses {refused_all} of them when you build ({refused} TypeScript cases and {traps_refused} traps).
